question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\text{E}[{X}^{2}+1].$

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.5$ | $0.25$ | $0.25$ |
question.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\sum }_{x\in S}r(x)f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={x}^{2}+1.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+1] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}+1\,f(x) \\  & =(4+1)\cdot 0.5+(1+1)\cdot 0.25+(1+1)\cdot 0.25 \\  & =5\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.25+2\cdot 0.25 \\  & =2.5+0.5+0.5 \\  & =3.5.\end{aligned}
$$
